name: Population Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public population and demographic data.

entries.title: Australian Bureau of Statistics Population
entries.description: The ABS population statistics topic: quarterly national, state and territory population estimates with components of change (natural increase, net overseas migration), regional population, projections, births, deaths and migration releases.

coverage.temporal: varies by release (estimates back to 1981 in the population clock; March 2026 quarter latest)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (ABS website copyright statement; excludes microdata, logos and third-party content)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The topic page lists releases including "Population clock and pyramid" ("population estimates back to 1981 and projections out to 2066") and "National, state and territory population" (released 17/09/2026): "Australia’s population was 27,921,150 people at 31 March 2026 ... Annual natural increase was 100,600 and net overseas migration was 292,100." It also lists "Deaths, Australia" (2/10/2026). Cadence is that of the headline national release; other releases on the page are annual. Formats and the ABS Data API weren't checked. Census of Population and Housing data live under abs.gov.au/census and aren't covered here.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the ABS copyright page (https://www.abs.gov.au/website-privacy-copyright-and-disclaimer) says "All material presented on this website is provided under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence, with the exception of: the Commonwealth Coat of Arms the ABS logo material protected by a trade mark unit record data (microdata) content supplied by third parties ...". The attribution format the ABS asks for wasn't captured, so the attribution string is the curator's.

entries.title: U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS)
entries.description: The Census Bureau's ongoing annual household survey producing detailed social, economic, housing and demographic estimates (1-year and 5-year) for the US and Puerto Rico, down to block groups for 5-year data. The main US source for population characteristics between censuses.

access.auth_note: The Census Data API offers a free key ("Request an API Key"); whether low-volume use needs one wasn't checked

coverage.spatial: United States and Puerto Rico (national, state, county, tract, block group)

entries.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl with a browser user agent). The banner says "2025 American Community Survey 1-year estimates and 2025 ACS 1-year Supplemental Estimates are now available." The page describes the ACS as "the premier source of detailed information about the nation's people and housing. As an ongoing survey conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau since 2005, the ACS collects detailed social, economic, housing, and demographic information from a sample of households across the 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico." The geography levels and formats are from general knowledge of data.census.gov and weren't checked. The ACS also carries housing characteristics, so a housing-almanac entry could overlap; this entry is scoped to population characteristics.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no data licence is stated on the page. The Census Bureau is a federal agency and its works are not copyrightable under 17 U.S.C. 105. The citation policy (https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html) asks users to "cite the Census Bureau as the source of the original data".

entries.title: U.S. Census Bureau Decennial Census of Population and Housing
entries.description: The constitutionally mandated count of every resident of the United States every ten years, used for congressional apportionment and redistricting, with detailed demographic and housing tables down to the census block. The 2020 Census is the latest.

access.auth_note: The Census Data API offers a free key ("Request an API Key"); whether low-volume use needs one wasn't checked

coverage.spatial: United States and Puerto Rico (national down to census block)

entries.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, Decennial Census of Population and Housing
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl with a browser user agent; no headless browser needed). The page reads "The U.S. Census Bureau counts each resident of the country, where they live on April 1, every ten years ending in zero. The Constitution mandates the enumeration to determine how to apportion the House of Representatives among the states." It says "The 2020 Census marked the 24th count of the U.S. population" and "Planning is currently underway for the 2030 Census". The schema has no decennial cadence, so it's irregular. The temporal range is inferred from "24th count" and wasn't checked against historical data availability. The formats and the API are assumed from data.census.gov and the Census Data API, which weren't probed.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no data licence is stated on the page. The Census Bureau is a federal agency and its works are not copyrightable under 17 U.S.C. 105. The citation policy (https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html) asks users to "cite the Census Bureau as the source of the original data".

entries.title: Eurostat Population and Demography Database
entries.description: Eurostat's population statistics for the EU, EFTA and candidate countries: population on 1 January, births, deaths and migration as components of change, population projections, and the population and housing census (Census Hub) results.

coverage.spatial: EU member states, EFTA and candidate countries (national and NUTS regions)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The theme page "Population and demography" has sub-sections "Population and housing censuses" (with Census Hub), "Demography, population stock and balance" and "Population projections", each with a Database page. The suggested URL /web/population-demography/database returned HTTP 404, so the theme overview is cataloged; the demography database page is https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/population-demography/demography-population-stock-balance/database (HTTP 200), which lists selected and detailed datasets. Releases, start years and NUTS levels weren't checked. The formats and the API/bulk access are from Eurostat's site-wide data tools (Web services, Bulk download in the menu) and weren't checked per dataset.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says editorial content "is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence" and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged." This matches the licence string used for Eurostat entries in the other verticals.

entries.title: Human Mortality Database
entries.description: Harmonized population estimates, exposures-to-risk, death counts, death rates and period and cohort life tables for about 40 mainly high-income countries, built from national vital statistics and censuses. The standard research source for long-run mortality and population-at-risk series.
entries.publisher: Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research, University of California, Berkeley, and French Institute for Demographic Studies (INED)

access.auth_note: Free registration (name, e-mail, affiliation) and acceptance of the HMD user agreement are required before downloading data; users registered before 15 June 2022 must register again

coverage.spatial: about 40 countries or areas, mainly Europe, North America, East Asia and Oceania
coverage.temporal: varies by country (some series start in the 18th or 19th century)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (HMD user agreement; HMD-constructed data only — input data remain under each provider's licence)
entries.attribution: HMD. Human Mortality Database. Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research (Germany), University of California, Berkeley (USA), and French Institute for Demographic Studies (France). Available at www.mortality.org (data downloaded on [date], DOI: 10.4054/HMD.Countries.[version code]).
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The home page says "The Human Mortality Database (HMD) is the world's leading scientific data resource on mortality in developed countries. The HMD provides detailed high-quality harmonized mortality and population estimates" and "The HMD follows open data principles." It lists summary-indicator Excel tables (infant mortality, survival to 65, life expectancy, population), zipped data files and a "Data by country or area" list (Australia, Austria, Belarus, Belgium ...). The country count, time spans and txt format are from general knowledge of the HMD and weren't checked; the latest release date wasn't captured. Included here for population estimates and exposures; mortality as a health outcome stays with health-almanac (CDC NVSS, WHO mortality database), and this entry doesn't duplicate them.
Registration: the FAQ (https://www.mortality.org/Project/FAQ) says "We require you to register before accessing the data in order to obtain basic contact information (i.e., your name, e-mail address, affiliation, and title)", and the login page says that users from before June 15, 2022 "will need to register again ... and accept the new user agreement before being able to download HMD data".
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the User Agreement (https://www.mortality.org/Data/UserAgreement) says "The HMD data are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License" and "The data constructed by the HMD team are published under the CC BY 4.0 license. This is not the case for the input data (for all HMD data series) which remain under each provider's distribution license." The attribution is the suggested citation from https://www.mortality.org/Research/CitationGuidelines.

entries.title: IBGE Censo Demográfico 2022
entries.description: Brazil's 2022 Census of Population, the largest in Latin America: population counts and the results of the universe and sample questionnaires (households, age and sex, Indigenous and quilombola populations, education, work, migration and more), with tables, microdata and documentation.
entries.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)

access.auth_note: Public-use microdata need no account; the page also lists controlled-access ("Acesso controlado") and restricted-access ("Acesso restrito") microdata, whose conditions were not checked.

coverage.spatial: Brazil (national, states, municipalities and finer census geographies)

entries.license: unverified — IBGE's "Termo de Uso e Política de Privacidade" covers portal use and personal data, not data reuse; the site footer says "© 2026 IBGE - Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística"
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01 in headless Chromium (new headless mode, playwright chromium.launch with channel "chromium"): HTTP 200, page "Censo 2022 | IBGE". curl, plain and with a browser User-Agent, got HTTP 403, so the vertical needs reachability.headless: true. The page is IBGE's statistics page for the Censo Demográfico, with tabs "Censo 2022", "Microdados", "Sobre a publicação", "Tabelas", "Conceitos e métodos", "Downloads" and "Notícias e Releases". Microdata are split into "Acesso público", "Acesso controlado" and "Acesso restrito", with documentation, weighting areas and a layout/dictionary. The page also states IBGE's data revision policy for the operation. The census project site, https://censo2022.ibge.gov.br/ (the issue's URL, also HTTP 200 in headless Chromium), carries news and releases: "Brasil tem 207,8 milhões de habitantes, mostra prévia do Censo 2022", "IBGE disponibiliza microdados da amostra do Censo 2022 com novo modelo e reforço à confidencialidade" (31/08/2026), and an announced release on 18 June 2026 of "Etnias e línguas indígenas: Resultados do universo (2ª edição)". This entry points at the statistics page because that is where tables and microdata are kept. File formats, SIDRA table access and the API were not checked, so format is left empty. It complements brazil-ibge-pnad-continua in labor-almanac.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. IBGE's "Termo de Uso e Política de Privacidade para Serviços do Portal do IBGE" (https://www.ibge.gov.br/acesso-informacao/acoes-e-programas/politica-de-privacidade.html, read in headless Chromium) deals with portal use and personal data and mentions intellectual property only in general terms. I found no statement granting reuse of IBGE data, so no licence is asserted. The page footer reads "© 2026 IBGE - Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística", a site-wide notice, not a data licence. The attribution string follows Brazilian convention and is not a quoted IBGE requirement.

entries.title: INEGI Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020
entries.description: Mexico's 2020 Population and Housing Census, which counted the population living in Mexico and its main demographic, socioeconomic and cultural characteristics. INEGI publishes general results, tabulations, microdata and open data.
entries.publisher: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI)
entries.license: INEGI Términos de Libre Uso de la Información (free use with attribution)
entries.attribution: Fuente: INEGI, Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31 in headless Chromium: HTTP 200. A curl with a browser user agent got HTTP 403, so the vertical should probe it headless. The page says "El Censo de Población y Vivienda 2020 (Censo 2020) se realizó del 2 al 27 de marzo" and that interviewers visited every dwelling "para obtener información sobre estas, contar a la población que vive en México e indagar sobre sus principales características demográficas, socioeconómicas y culturales". Tabs read "Resultados generales, Documentación, Tabulados, Microdatos, Datos abiertos, Publicaciones, Herramientas". It's a one-off census edition, so cadence is static; the geography levels and the formats are assumed and weren't checked. The 2020 census also feeds the education-almanac entry mexico-inegi-caracteristicas-educativas, which covers education topics only.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: INEGI's Términos de Libre Uso (https://www.inegi.org.mx/inegi/terminos.html, read in headless Chromium) allow reuse, including as input to other products, and require "Debe otorgar los créditos correspondientes al INEGI como autor, y cuando técnicamente sea posible, mencionar la fuente de extracción de la información de la siguiente manera: “Fuente: INEGI, nombre del producto de donde se extrae la información”". This is INEGI's general information-use licence rather than a census-specific one.

entries.title: IPUMS International
entries.description: Harmonized census and survey microdata from national statistical offices worldwide (104 countries, 656 censuses and surveys, over 1 billion person records), integrated by the University of Minnesota so variables are comparable across countries and years.

access.auth_note: Free individual registration with a described research project, reviewed by IPUMS, and acceptance of the IPUMS International Usage License; each team member must apply and be licensed individually

coverage.temporal: varies by country (historical and modern census rounds)

entries.license: restricted — IPUMS International Usage License (no redistribution; scholarly research and education only; no commercial use)
entries.attribution: IPUMS International, Minnesota Population Center, University of Minnesota, plus the national statistical offices that produced each sample (see the citation page for the versioned citation)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page says "IPUMS International is dedicated to collecting and distributing census microdata from around the world" and that the project aims to "harmonize data, and disseminate the harmonized data free of charge", with "104 countries – 656 censuses and surveys – over 1 billion person records" and "Source data for IPUMS International are generously provided by participating National Statistical Offices." Data come as custom extracts built online. The extract formats (fixed-width with syntax files, csv) are assumed and weren't checked. Jurisdiction is national/US because the publisher is a US university, as the other verticals do for university-run sources; the coverage is global. It's run by a university, not a federal agency, so it isn't US Gov public domain.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the registration form (https://uma.pop.umn.edu/ipumsi/user/new, read in headless Chromium) carries the "IPUMS INTERNATIONAL USAGE LICENSE": "Redistribution: You will not redistribute the data ... Under IPUMS International agreements with collaborating agencies, redistribution of the data to third parties is prohibited. Each member of a research team using the data must apply for access and be licensed individually. Usage: You agree to use IPUMS International data for scholarly research and educational purposes only. Commercial use is strictly prohibited." The form says the project description "will be used to evaluate your application". The citation page (https://international.ipums.org/international/citation.shtml) says publications "must cite it appropriately" and "Researchers should also acknowledge the statistical agencies that originally produced the data"; the exact versioned citation text wasn't captured.

Accordingly the terms of use does not apply to such data, and said data may be used freely." It adds "The Terms of Use was established on March 7, 2025. The Terms of Use is based on the Public Data License (Version 1.0)" and "The Terms of Use are compatible with the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0". The source-citation example is the basis of the attribution string.

coverage.spatial: South Africa (national and sub-national, via Stats by Location)

entries.license: unverified — Stats SA standard copyright notice (reuse with acknowledgement, no sale without permission), seen in a Stats SA publication, not on the census portal

Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The portal is a JavaScript app (plain curl returns only the title "Statistics South Africa | Census Dissemination"), so it was read in headless Chromium, which landed on https://census.statssa.gov.za/#/. It reads "Welcome to the official Stats SA Census Portal" and "Census 2022 was the first digital population count", shows "Total population: 62 027 503" and "Number of households: 17 828 778", and has year tabs for 2022, 2011, 2001 and 1996 plus "Stats by Location" and "Stats by Theme". Stats SA's Work Programme 2026/27 (https://www.statssa.gov.za/strategy_plan/Work_Programme_2026_27.pdf) carries the agency's standard notice: "Users may apply or process this data, provided Statistics South Africa (Stats SA) is acknowledged as the original source of the data; that it is specified that the application and/or analysis is the result of the user’s independent processing of the data; and that neither the basic data nor any reprocessed version or application thereof may be sold or offered for sale in any form whatsoever without prior permission from Stats SA." entries.title: UN DESA International Migrant Stock
entries.description: United Nations estimates of the number of international migrants by sex, age, country of destination and country of origin for 233 countries and areas, 1990-2024. The reference series for migration as a component of population.
entries.publisher: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division
entries.license: CC-BY-3.0-IGO (copyright statement inside the 2024 data files)
entries.attribution: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). International Migrant Stock 2024.
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page heads "International Migrant Stock 2024" and says the 2024 edition "presents the latest United Nations estimates of the numbers and characteristics of international migrants around the world. Covering the period from 1990 to 2024 ... for 233 countries and areas." It links Excel files for total, age and sex, and destination and origin, with older editions (2019, 2017 and earlier) below. Editions are irregular (about every 2-5 years).
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the page itself only carries the un.org footer (Copyright, Terms of Use). The 2024 data file undesa_pd_2024_ims_stock_by_sex_and_destination.xlsx (downloaded from the page's link, HTTP 200 with a browser user agent, 403 without one) states "Copyright © 2024 by United Nations, made available under a Creative Commons license CC BY 3.0 IGO: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/igo/" and gives the suggested citation "United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024)." Only that one file was opened; the others are assumed to carry the same statement. The attribution's dataset title is added by the curator. Migration flows (a separate UN dataset) are not covered here.

entries.title: UN DESA World Population Prospects
entries.description: The United Nations' official population estimates (1950-present) and projections to 2100 for 237 countries or areas, by single year of age and sex, with fertility, mortality and net migration indicators. The standard global reference for population size and structure.

entries.attribution: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024, Online Edition.
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31 in headless Chromium: HTTP 200. A plain curl also got HTTP 200 but the page body is rendered by JavaScript, so the text was read in the browser. The page says "The 2024 Revision of World Population Prospects is the twenty-eighth edition of official United Nations population estimates and projections" and that it "presents population estimates from 1950 to the present for 237 countries or areas" and projections "to the year 2100". The 2024 revision was the latest seen. The page mentions Excel files, CSV bulk download and a Data Portal with "an open API"; the API page (https://population.un.org/dataportalapi/index.html) says "our data endpoints require an authorization token for access", hence the auth_note. Revisions come every two years or so, which the schema can't express, so cadence is irregular.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the downloads page (https://population.un.org/wpp/downloads) states "Copyright © 2024 by United Nations, made available under a Creative Commons license CC BY 3.0 IGO: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/igo/" followed by the suggested citation used as attribution here. The API page also names CC BY 3.0 IGO. Formats beyond xlsx/csv/json and the start of the probabilistic outputs weren't checked.

entries.title: UN Statistics Division Demographic Yearbook
entries.description: The United Nations Demographic Yearbook: official national statistics on population size and composition, censuses, births, deaths, marriages and divorces, compiled annually from national statistical offices since 1948, with special census-topic issues.

coverage.spatial: global (national data reported by countries or areas)

entries.license: unverified — no data-specific licence on the DYB page; its footer links the un.org Terms of Use (personal, non-commercial); the UNdata mirror's terms allow free redistribution with citation
entries.attribution: United Nations Statistics Division, Demographic Yearbook
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page lists "Demographic Yearbook (DYB) Regular Issues 2021 - 2024" with "DYB 2024 - individual tables & notes - Download a copy (pdf 16.0MB)", annual issues back to 1948-1959, special census-round issues, and country metadata for population estimates, vital statistics and population and housing censuses. DYB 2024 is the latest issue seen. Births and deaths here are population inputs; vital statistics as health outcomes belong to health-almanac. The format list is from link labels (pdf); the xlsx for individual tables is assumed and wasn't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the DYB page links only to http://www.un.org/en/aboutun/copyright/ and http://www.un.org/en/aboutun/terms/. The un.org Terms of Use (https://www.un.org/en/about-us/terms-of-use) grant permission "to download and copy the information ... for the User's personal, non-commercial use, without any right to resell or redistribute them". DYB tables are also served through UNdata, whose terms (https://data.un.org/Host.aspx?Content=UNdataUse) say "All data and metadata provided on UNdata's website are available free of charge and may be copied freely, duplicated and further distributed provided that UNdata is cited as the reference." The two conflict, and neither is DYB-specific, so the licence is left unverified.
